subject: Encryption & KMS follow-up / PayWise discovery
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@paywise.com>, Tom Keller <tom.keller@paywise.com>
Cc: nikhil.sharma@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Recap & next steps — encryption, KMS, and data residency (PayWise)

Alicia / Tom — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of PayWise requirements (as we understood them):
- PII scope: user names, email addresses, last 4 of account numbers for analytics
- Data residency: EU for EU customers; US for US customers (multi-region support required)
- Retention: transactional logs retained 7 years; user-level PII for 3 years, with delete-on-request
- Logging: request/response metadata required for audit, but PayWise cannot retain raw prompt text beyond 30 days
- Encryption: in-transit TLS 1.2+ required; at-rest encryption with customer-managed keys (BYOK/KMS) preferred; HSM options for signing would be evaluated

Open questions we noted:
1) For BYOK, do you require a KMS hosted in PayWise VPC (customer-managed KMS in your cloud) or will a Redwood-hosted customer key (Redwood KMS with CMK scoped to your account) suffice?
2) For HSM-backed keys, is FIPS 140-2 Level 3 required or is Level 2 acceptable?
3) Which logs (if any) need to be masked vs. fully omitted from Redwood retention?
4) Does PayWise require field-level encryption for specific PII fields in addition to disk-level encryption?

Proposed next steps: 
- Marissa: Share our SOC2 summary and KMS integration guide (attached) + a short matrix of options (Redwood-managed CMK, customer-managed KMS, HSM-backed) — by EOD tomorrow.
- Alicia: Confirm whether PayWise prefers in-VPC BYOK or Redwood-hosted CMK for the initial pilot.
- Technical follow-up call: propose Wed 26 Nov 10am PT to walk the KMS flow and look at sample logs masking configs.

Attachments: SOC2-Summary-PayWise.pdf, KMS-Integration-Guide.pdf (see attached).

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
Redwood Inference

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@paywise.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Keller <tom.keller@paywise.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — encryption, KMS, and data residency (PayWise)

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few quick answers from our side: 

- BYOK preference: For the pilot, PayWise prefers Redwood-hosted CMK integrated with our KMS via customer key import (we don't want to manage KMS lifecycle for the first phase). For production, we will likely require a KMS in our AWS account (BYOK with key policies controlled by PayWise).
- HSM: FIPS 140-2 Level 3 is preferred for production; Level 2 acceptable for non-prod.
- Logs: We need request metadata (timestamps, model id, tokens billed) for audits, but must redact raw prompt text after 30 days. For any PII-containing prompts, we prefer stripping the PII server-side before retention.
- Field-level encryption: Yes — account number fragments (last 4) must be stored only in hashed form in analytics exports.

Tom and I can be on the tech call Wed 26 Nov 10am PT. Could you include someone from engineering to cover the KMS integration flow?

Alicia
Alicia Gomez | Head of Security Compliance, PayWise
Alicia.Gomez@paywise.com

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: KMS options for PayWise (notes)

Marissa — quick internal notes ahead of the 10am call: 

- Option A (fastest pilot): Redwood-managed CMK per customer (we generate CMK, keys stored in our KMS/HSM, we provide dedicated key access controls). Pros: fastest to onboard, supports key rotation, Redwood handles HSM. Cons: PayWise may push back for production.
- Option B (BYOK - customer KMS in AWS/GCP): We integrate with PayWise KMS via role-based access (we never hold plaintext keys). We'll need a trust relationship and a short-lived crypto-material fetch or use envelope encryption where PayWise decrypts only within their boundary. Pros: meets BYOK requirement; Cons: more ops + networking (VPC peering or private link) for key fetch path inferences.
- Option C (HSM-backed external): Support HSM signing via CloudHSM/Thales. Requires extra certs and separate onboarding; target for prod only.

Operational notes: masking at ingestion + prompt transformation is doable client-side or via Redwood pre-processing hook. We should propose a masking pipeline for PII before logs hit retention.

I'll be on the technical call. Rishi — can you bring the KMS integration guide and a simple diagram?

-Nikhil

Alicia / Tom — great to meet yesterday. Thanks for confirming your preferences in advance of the pilot. Attaching the SOC2 summary and our KMS integration guide (also shared via Drive link below).

Next steps & timeline: 
- Pilot: Redwood-hosted CMK with customer-imported key material for the pilot (we will not persist your plaintext keys). Proposal: 2-week pilot starting 1 Dec — we'll provide a sandbox tenant and a short checklist for key import.
- Production: BYOK in PayWise AWS account + HSM-backed keys (FIPS 140-2 Level 3). We'll scope network private connectivity (AWS PrivateLink or VPC peering) in the SOW.
- Logging & retention: We will configure automatic prompt redaction and a 30-day window for prompt text. Audit metadata (timestamps, model, token metrics) will be retained per your retention policy (7 years for transactional logs).

Action items: 
- PayWise: confirm pilot start date (Marissa will provision sandbox once confirmed).
- PayWise: share an initial contact for your cloud security engineer (Tom?) so we can coordinate KMS key import steps.
- Redwood: Nikhil and Rishi to provide the sandbox checklist and short diagram of encryption flow (by Mon 30 Nov).
